newsitem.title: UK: Utd Assurance to cut 2200 jobs as profits up.
newsitem.headline: Utd Assurance to cut 2200 jobs as profits up.

text.p: Britain's United Assurance Group, formed by the merger of Refuge Group and United Friendly last October, on Thursday announced it was cutting 2,200 jobs as a result of the integration of the two businesses.
The layoffs, higher than the 1800 redundancies the group predicted by the company in August will involve the closure of over half the group's regional offices.
Cost savings are forecast to amount to around 37 million pounds ($60.7 million) a year.
United's chief executive George Mack said that the opportunities to make cost savings and achieve economies of scale were essential in enabling it to compete in its chosen businesses.
The rationalisation and integration will involve an eventual reduction in the group's regional and branch offices to 116 from 279.
United has set aside 76.3 million pounds for the expected integration costs.
The new structure would enable greater emphasis to be placed on clients' needs, the company said.
The news of the lay-offs came as the merged group announced pre-tax profits of 549.3 million pounds for 1996, including 371.3 million pounds in exceptional items.
Before these, profits from continuing operations were up 18 percent at 193.5 million pounds.
The dividend for the year was raised 35 percent to 18 pence per share. And the company told industry analysts that more staff reductions could emerge in the future. ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
